problems.name: Set Matrix Zeroes
problems.question: Given an m x n integer matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0 in place.

examples.explanation: The zero at row 1, column 1 clears that row and column.
Zeros in the first row must still clear their columns.
There is no zero to propagate.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(1). First row and first column store marker flags.

problems.name: Spiral Matrix
problems.question: Given an m x n matrix, return all elements of the matrix in spiral order.

examples.explanation: The outer layer is read before the center.
The final inner row is handled once.
One column is already spiral order.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(1) excluding output. Shrinking boundaries avoid visited state.

problems.name: Spiral Matrix II
problems.question: Given an integer n, generate an n x n matrix filled with numbers from 1 to n^2 in spiral order.

examples.explanation: Values are written around the boundary then inward.
Only one cell is filled.
The single layer contains four values.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Boundary-layer filling writes each cell once.

problems.name: Rotate Image
problems.question: Given an n x n matrix, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise in place.

examples.explanation: Rows become columns after clockwise rotation.
All four layers rotate in place.
One cell is unchanged.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(1). Transpose then reverse each row.

problems.name: Search a 2D Matrix
problems.question: Given a matrix where each row is sorted and the first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row, return whether target exists.

examples.explanation: 3 is present in the first row.
13 is between values but absent.
Single-cell matrix contains the target.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(log(mn)); Space O(1). Binary search a flattened virtual array.

problems.name: Search a 2D Matrix II
problems.question: Given an m x n matrix sorted ascending left-to-right in each row and top-to-bottom in each column, return whether target exists.

examples.explanation: The target is found while walking the staircase.
The search eliminates all candidates.
Single row still supports staircase movement.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(m+n); Space O(1). Staircase search eliminates one row or column each step.

problems.name: Game of Life
problems.question: Given a board of live and dead cells, update it to the next Game of Life state in place using the standard four rules.

examples.explanation: Cells update simultaneously from the original board.
The dead bottom-right cell becomes live.
A single dead cell stays dead.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(1). Transitional values encode old and new states in place.

problems.name: Word Search
problems.question: Given an m x n board of characters and a word, return true if the word exists by moving horizontally or vertically without reusing a cell.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 6; 1 <= word.length <= 15; board and word contain English letters.

examples.explanation: A valid path spells the word.
The word appears through adjacent cells.
The path would need to reuse B.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn * 4^L); Space O(L). In-place marking avoids a visited matrix.

problems.name: Number of Islands
problems.question: Given a grid of 1s and 0s, return the number of islands where land is connected horizontally or vertically.

examples.explanation: All land cells connect into one island.
There are three disconnected land components.
No land means no island.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn) worst-case queue. Mutate visited land to water.

problems.name: Max Area of Island
problems.question: Given a binary grid, return the maximum area of an island connected horizontally or vertically.

examples.explanation: The connected component has four land cells.
There is no island.
The whole grid is one island.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn) worst-case queue. Mutate visited land to water.

problems.name: Surrounded Regions
problems.question: Given a board of X and O, capture all regions of O that are fully surrounded by X.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 200; board[i][j] is X or O.

examples.explanation: Only the boundary-connected O remains.
Single cell remains unchanged.
Every O touches the boundary.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn) queue. Flood fill safe boundary-connected cells first.

problems.name: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.question: Given a matrix of heights, return coordinates from which water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans.

examples.explanation: These cells can reach both oceans.
The only cell touches both oceans.
Flat terrain can flow everywhere.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Reverse BFS/DFS from ocean borders.

problems.name: Flood Fill
problems.question: Given an image, a starting cell, and a new color, recolor the connected component with the same original color.

examples.explanation: Only the connected 1-component is recolored.
No work is needed when the color is unchanged.
The single component is one cell.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn) queue. Recolor cells directly to mark visited.

problems.name: 01 Matrix
problems.question: Given a binary matrix, return a matrix where each cell contains the distance to the nearest 0.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 10000 total cells; mat[i][j] is 0 or 1; at least one zero exists.

examples.explanation: The center one is adjacent to zeros.
Distances expand from all zeros.
Zero distance for the only cell.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Multi-source BFS visits each cell once.

problems.name: Rotting Oranges
problems.question: Given a grid of empty cells, fresh oranges, and rotten oranges, return minutes until all oranges rot or -1 if impossible.

examples.explanation: Fresh oranges rot level by level.
One fresh orange is isolated.
No fresh oranges exist.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Multi-source BFS processes each orange once.

problems.name: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
problems.question: Given an n x n binary grid, return the length of the shortest clear path from top-left to bottom-right moving in 8 directions.

examples.explanation: Move diagonally from start to end.
BFS finds the shortest clear path.
The starting cell is blocked.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). BFS visits each open cell at most once.

problems.name: Toeplitz Matrix
problems.question: Given a matrix, return true if every diagonal from top-left to bottom-right has the same value.

examples.explanation: Every diagonal repeats the same value.
The main diagonal contains 1 and 2.
A single cell is Toeplitz.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(1). Compare each cell to its top-left neighbor.

problems.name: Valid Sudoku
problems.question: Given a partially filled 9 x 9 Sudoku board, return true if it is valid under row, column, and 3 x 3 box constraints.
problems.constraints: board.length == 9; board[i].length == 9; board[i][j] is digit 1-9 or dot.

examples.explanation: No row, column, or box has duplicate digits.

examples.input: board has two 8s in the first column
examples.explanation: Column uniqueness is violated.
No filled digit violates constraints.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(81); Space O(1). Bit masks track used digits per row, column, and box.

problems.name: Sudoku Solver
problems.question: Given a 9 x 9 Sudoku board, fill it so every row, column, and 3 x 3 box contains digits 1 through 9 exactly once.
problems.constraints: board.length == 9; board[i].length == 9; board has exactly one valid solution.

examples.explanation: Backtracking fills every dot with a valid digit.

examples.input: board has one dot in a row
examples.explanation: Only one candidate satisfies constraints.
No empty cell requires branching.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(9^E); Space O(E). Bit masks make constraint checks O(1).

problems.name: Diagonal Traverse
problems.question: Given an m x n matrix, return all elements in diagonal order alternating up-right and down-left.

examples.explanation: Direction alternates between diagonals.
The middle diagonal is reversed.
A single row has no vertical movement.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(1) excluding output. Simulate direction and bounce at boundaries.
